html:
The Beja are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Red Sea hills and the desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, in what are now Sudan, Egypt and Eritrea. The map shows their lands in its 900 snapshot.

They were nomads who herded camels, sheep and cattle, and they controlled the routes to the gold mines of the eastern desert. Many historians link them with the Blemmyes who raided Roman Egypt.

In the 800s they clashed with the Abbasid governors of Egypt over the gold mines, and in 831 they were forced to accept a treaty. Arab miners and traders moved into their land. The Beja stayed between the Muslim north and Christian Makuria on the Nile, and slowly became Muslim over the following centuries. Their own language, Bedawi, is still spoken.
